source_notes.label: Shared precursor preparation, distinct solvent conditions
source_notes.summary: Every final solvent route retains the stated 6 g Ti(SO4)2, 0.2 M solution, 3 M ammonia to pH 7.5, 20 h aging, filtrate conductivity strictly below 100 μs/cm, 125 mL selected solvent, 0.5 h ultrasound, 2.5 mL 30 wt% H2O2 in an ice bath, 78°C 4 h reflux and 120°C 15 h solvothermal treatment. Unknown volumes, ramps and pressure remain unknown.

source_notes.label: Before-treatment evidence is not a final-product result
source_notes.summary: Figures 1–3 panels a, b show water/ethanol precursors before solvothermal treatment: yellow aqueous colloid or straw-yellow ethanol precipitate, mainly amorphous. Panels c–i are after treatment. Precursor FTIR 900 cm−1 signal is assigned to the aqueous peroxo group; absence/persistence wording does not quantify an exact residual concentration.

source_notes.label: Labeled table mapping retains the contradictory prose order
source_notes.summary: Table 1 explicitly assigns each TEM/XRD/area/zeta/activity value to TW, TWE4, TWE1, TWE0.25, TE. The preceding Figure 2 e–i order and prose Scherrer list conflict. The table assignment remains explicit alongside that conflict; the narrative 9.0 nm endpoint does not replace Table 1 9.7 nm.

source_notes.label: Lengths, widths, particles and crystallites remain separate
source_notes.summary: TW is described as rods about 80×7 nm; TE as rectangles about 26×14 nm. Table 1 DTEM 80.6 and 26.1 nm are source diameter metrics, whereas 13.4 and 11.8 nm are Scherrer crystallite estimates. HRTEM 3.4/4.8 Å source assignments are retained literally and do not establish a measured unit-cell model.

source_notes.label: Poor solvent controls are not omitted or promoted to successes
source_notes.summary: Pure n-propanol and n-butanol yield poorly crystalline aggregated material with amorphous floccus-like morphology. They share the explicit method but have no assigned numeric size or catalytic result and were excluded from the photocatalysis study.

source_notes.label: Catalytic outcome belongs to an additionally dried specimen
source_notes.summary: Catalysts were rotary-evaporated 45°C then dried 110°C 1 h. The assay uses 10 mg/L phenol, 1 g/L TiO2, 75 mL in an 80 mL tube, dark 30 min, 365 nm 16 W UV with stirring. Table 1 contains 6 h efficiencies. The no-catalyst blank and catechol explanation stay qualitative; curves were not digitized.
source_locators: Main pp. 2–5, Section 2.4, Section 3.3, Figure 5 and Table 1

source_notes.label: Growth mechanism remains an attributed interpretation
source_notes.summary: Equation 2 proposes peroxotitanate condensation and growth units; Scheme 1 attributes anisotropy to solvent/facet interactions. The scheme expressly does not depict real crystal lengths. Literature pH 3–9, methanol and 2-propanol discussions are explanatory context, not added experimental conditions or reagents for these recipes.
source_locators: Main pp. 4–5, Section 3.4, Equation 2 and Scheme 1

evidence_conflicts: Main p.3 lists Scherrer sizes 13.4, 11.0, 10.2, 8.9 and 11.8 nm after discussing Figure2 e–i, whose caption orders ethanol through water. Table1 instead explicitly labels these values TW, TWE4, TWE1, TWE0.25 and TE. Numeric sample assignments here follow the explicit Table1 row labels; the conflicting prose order is retained, not silently resolved.
Main pp.3 and5 describe the mixed-solvent TEM range as47.0 to9.0nm, while Table1 explicitly reports9.7nm for TWE0.25. The labeled table value remains9.7nm; no replacement by9.0nm.
Table1 calls DTEM a diameter even for rodlike TW and rectangular TE. Their separate approximate length/width descriptions are preserved and are not substituted for the table metric.

Main p.3 assigns the TW HRTEM spacings3.4 and4.8Å to(101) and(002), respectively; Figure4a visibly labels0.34nm and an(001) growth arrow. These source labels are retained without crystallographic correction or invented atomic coordinates.
Main p.5 describes [001] growth as approximately2.7 times[101] but prints G100≈2.7G101. Both notations are retained as source interpretation, not a measured growth-rate result.
Table1 and p.4 print the calculated-area expression S=6/d*ρ. The literal expression and author-derived status are preserved; no density value, operator correction or recomputation is introduced.
